record.original_question: Let S_m be the space of real 2 x m matrices, let L_1 and L_2 be self-adjoint positive-definite linear maps on S_m, let F_1,F_2 in S_m and c_1,c_2 in R define the two quadratic wells W_j(F)=(F-F_j)·L_j(F-F_j)+c_j, and let W(F)=min{W_1(F),W_2(F)}. Is the quasiconvex envelope QW of this two-well energy always equal to its rank-one convex envelope RW in two spatial dimensions, for every choice of m,L_1,L_2,F_1,F_2,c_1,c_2?

evidence.quote: Problem 1: Is rank convexity equal to quasiconvexity for the two well problem in two spatial dimen- sions?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let m ≥ 1 and let S_m denote the space of real 2×m matrices, equipped with the inner product F·G = tr(F G^T). Let L_1, L_2 : S_m → S_m be self-adjoint, positive-definite linear operators, fix matrices F_1, F_2 ∈ S_m and constants c_1, c_2 ∈ R, and define the two quadratic wells

  W_j(F) = (F − F_j) · L_j(F − F_j) + c_j,  j = 1,2,

together with the two-well energy density

  W(F) = min{ W_1(F), W_2(F) },  F ∈ S_m.

Recall that for a Borel function V : S_m → R bounded below:
• V is rank-one convex if t ↦ V(F + t a⊗b) is convex on R for every F ∈ S_m and every a ∈ R^2, b ∈ R^m;
• V is quasiconvex (in the sense of Morrey) if for every F ∈ S_m and every smooth, compactly supported φ : (0,1)^2 → R^m one has
  ∫_{(0,1)^2} V(F + ∇φ(x)) dx ≥ V(F);
• the rank-one convex envelope RV is the supremum of all rank-one convex functions ≤ V, and the quasiconvex envelope QV is the supremum of all quasiconvex functions ≤ V.

In general RV ≤ QV. Determine whether, for every choice of m, L_1, L_2, F_1, F_2, c_1, c_2 as above, the two-well density W on S_m satisfies

  QW = RW

identically on S_m.
artifact.category_tag: two-well quasiconvexification in calculus of variations
artifact.status_search_result: The general question of whether rank-one convexity equals quasiconvexity in two spatial dimensions (Morrey's conjecture for n=2) is widely regarded as a major open problem. For two-component maps (m=2) it has been argued to hold, and quadratic densities trivially satisfy the equivalence, but the two-well case for general target dimension m in 2D remains open: no proof of QW = RW in full generality and no counterexample are known.

status_evidence.title: Morrey's conjecture: rank-one convexity implies quasi-convexity for two-dimensional, two-component maps
status_evidence.snippet: The remaining question whether rank-one convexity implies quasiconvexity for n=2 is known as Morrey's problem.
status_evidence.claim: The 2D case of Morrey's conjecture (rank-one convexity vs quasiconvexity) is a major open problem; the two-component (m=2) case has been addressed.

status_evidence.title: Rank-one convexity does not imply quasiconvexity (Šverák)
status_evidence.snippet: Šverák's counterexample requires m ≥ 3, n ≥ 2; in particular, no such examples are known when n = 2 in full generality.
status_evidence.claim: In planar (n=2) elasticity the equivalence of rank-one convexity and quasiconvexity is not settled.
